title: Terra Incognita: Mapping the Antipodes before 1600
creator: Alfred Hiatt
publication_context: British Library / University of Chicago Press
role_in_essay: Establishes that the antipodal south is an argument before it is a coastline.
notes: The anchor for Act I's claim that the southern continent is inherited reasoning rather than report. Not yet read against the page for the specific propositions the act will make.

title: Antipodes: In Search of the Southern Continent
creator: Avan Judd Stallard
role_in_essay: The historiography of the southern continent as an idea, including its persistence after contrary evidence.
notes: Directly useful for the high-risk claim about what early modern cartographers can be said to have believed.

title: The Furthest Shore: Images of Terra Australis from the Middle Ages to Captain Cook
creator: William Eisler
role_in_essay: Bridges Act I to Act IV: the same imagined shore from cosmography through to Cook.
notes: Covers the whole arc the essay's first half needs, which makes it the source most worth reading first.

title: The History of Cartography, Volume 3: Cartography in the European Renaissance
creator: David Woodward (ed.)
role_in_essay: The authority on copying, plate reuse and the mechanics by which a coastline is inherited.
notes: Open access via the publisher's HOC pages. The chapters relevant to Act II have not yet been identified by number.

title: Trading Territories: Mapping the Early Modern World
creator: Jerry Brotton
role_in_essay: Why a printed coastline carries commercial and political authority independent of its evidence.
notes: Supporting rather than load-bearing; drop it if Act II can be argued from HOC III alone.

title: Epitome cosmografica, o compendiosa introduttione all'astronomia, geografia, & idrografia
creator: Vincenzo Maria Coronelli
publication_context: Cologne [i.e. Venice], at the request of Andrea Poletti
edition_state: 1693; copy and issue not yet established
role_in_essay: The textual half of Act III, including the section on the polar lands.
notes: A digitised copy was located during this audit but the volume has not been opened. The pages carrying 'Terre Polari, Artiche, ed Antartiche' are untranscribed, so no statement about what Coronelli writes there may yet be made.

title: Atlante Veneto
creator: Vincenzo Maria Coronelli
publication_context: Venice; thirteen folio volumes, conceived as a continuation of the Blaeu Atlas Maior
edition_state: Which volumes and states carry the polar material is not established
role_in_essay: The cartographic half of Act III and the publication context of the polar plates.
notes: Recorded as a work, not as a copy. Act III cannot cite the Atlante Veneto until a specific volume, plate and holding copy are named.

title: Vincenzo Coronelli Cosmographer (1650-1718)
creator: Marica Milanesi
role_in_essay: The scholarly control on every claim Act III makes about Coronelli's method and sources.
notes: Act III's highest-priority acquisition. Without it the act risks reading Coronelli's plates as if they were his opinions.

short_title: Cook, Voyage towards the South Pole
title: A Voyage towards the South Pole and Round the World
creator: James Cook
publication_context: London: W. Strahan and T. Cadell, two volumes
role_in_essay: The published voyage whose charts and text turn a failure to find land into a bounded blank.
notes: The official account that carries the 1777 southern-hemisphere chart. No page locators are transcribed.

title: The Journals of Captain James Cook on his Voyages of Discovery, Volume II: The Voyage of the Resolution and Adventure, 1772-1775
creator: J. C. Beaglehole (ed.)
role_in_essay: The scholarly edition against which any quotation from the second voyage must be checked.
notes: Act IV should argue from Beaglehole rather than from the 1777 publication where the two differ, and should say so where it matters.

title: Bellingshausen and the Russian Antarctic Expedition, 1819-21
creator: Rip Bulkeley
role_in_essay: The control on every priority statement the essay makes about 1820.
notes: Act V's most important secondary source, because the priority question is where this essay is most likely to repeat a national myth by accident.

title: The Voyage of Captain Bellingshausen to the Antarctic Seas, 1819-1821
creator: Frank Debenham (ed.)
role_in_essay: The English text through which the essay would read Bellingshausen's sightings.
notes: A translation is an interpretation. If Act V rests a priority claim on wording, the Russian text has to be consulted or the dependence on Debenham declared.

short_title: Weddell, Voyage towards the South Pole
title: A Voyage towards the South Pole, performed in the years 1822-24
creator: James Weddell
publication_context: London: Longman, Hurst, Rees, Orme, Brown and Green
role_in_essay: The open-water penetration of the sea later named for him, and a case where one season's ice is mistaken for a permanent condition.
notes: Also a ghost-geography source: Weddell's reported islands need checking against later disproof.

short_title: Ross, Voyage of Discovery and Research
title: A Voyage of Discovery and Research in the Southern and Antarctic Regions, during the years 1839-43
creator: James Clark Ross
role_in_essay: The survey that converts scattered sightings into charted coast, and the disproof of several Wilkes positions.
notes: Ross sailing over land Wilkes had charted is the cleanest single episode joining Act V to Act VI.

title: Narrative of the United States Exploring Expedition, during the years 1838-1842
creator: Charles Wilkes
publication_context: Philadelphia: Lea and Blanchard, five volumes and atlas
role_in_essay: A continental claim advanced with charted coast, parts of which were later sailed through.
notes: Wilkes must not be presented simply as wrong. Which of his positions survived and which did not is exactly the distinction Act VI is for.

title: Below the Convergence: Voyages toward Antarctica, 1699-1839
creator: Alan Gurney
role_in_essay: Narrative synthesis of the sealing and exploring voyages between Cook and Ross.
notes: Useful for sequence and context; not authoritative enough to settle a priority claim on its own.

short_title: Ramsay, No Longer on the Map
title: No Longer on the Map: Discovering Places That Never Were
creator: Raymond H. Ramsay
role_in_essay: A general treatment of cartographic features that were later removed.
notes: Popular rather than scholarly. Usable for orientation, not as the authority for any individual disproof.

title: Phantom Islands of the Atlantic
creator: Donald S. Johnson
role_in_essay: Method: how a reported island survives on charts and how it is eventually removed.
notes: Atlantic rather than Antarctic, and cited for the pattern rather than for any southern feature.

title: A Chronology of Antarctic Exploration: A Synopsis of Events and Activities from the Earliest Times until the International Polar Years, 2007-09
creator: Robert K. Headland
role_in_essay: The dating spine for Acts V to VII and the first check on any date this programme publishes.
notes: The single most useful reference for the chronology tables. Every date in the dataset should eventually carry a Headland entry or a reason it does not.

title: South: The Story of Shackleton's Last Expedition, 1914-1917
creator: Ernest Shackleton
role_in_essay: The expedition's own account, including the plan Act VIII contrasts with the drift.
notes: Ghost-written in part and shaped for publication. Positions taken from it are Shackleton's published positions, not Worsley's workings.

title: Shackleton's Boat Journey
creator: Frank Arthur Worsley
role_in_essay: The navigator's own account of the James Caird passage and its observational constraints.
notes: Written twenty-five years after the events. Where it conflicts with the contemporary log the log wins, and the essay must say which it is using.

title: Endurance: An Epic of Polar Adventure
creator: Frank Arthur Worsley
role_in_essay: Worsley's fuller account of the drift year, including the ship's loss.
notes: The reported sinking position enters the literature through accounts of this kind; the coordinate's provenance is exactly what the Coda is about.

title: The Endurance: Shackleton's Legendary Antarctic Expedition
creator: Caroline Alexander
publication_context: New York: Alfred A. Knopf, with the Hurley photographs
role_in_essay: Reliable modern narrative and the standard account of the photographic record.
notes: Narrative context only. No position in the dataset should rest on it.

title: A History of Nautical Astronomy
creator: Charles H. Cotter
role_in_essay: What a sight, a chronometer and a dead-reckoning run could and could not deliver in 1915.
notes: The technical basis for the Coda's uncertainty argument. Needed before any error figure is published.

title: Endurance22 expedition: discovery of the wreck of Endurance
creator: Falklands Maritime Heritage Trust
role_in_essay: The 2022 location and the search that produced it.
notes: The expedition site returned 403 to this audit, so nothing here is transcribed from it. The Coda's comparison of the 1915 and 2022 positions is unsupported until a citable published position and its uncertainty are read.

title: Historic Site and Monument No. 93: Wreck of Endurance
creator: Antarctic Treaty Consultative Meeting
role_in_essay: The designated coordinates as an official record rather than a news figure.
notes: The preferred authority for the wreck position because it is a treaty instrument. The entry could not be retrieved during this audit and is logged as a gap.

title: Historical GIS: Technologies, Methodologies and Scholarship
creator: Ian N. Gregory and Paul S. Ell
role_in_essay: Method reference for representing incomplete and uncertain historical geography.
notes: Cited for the data model rather than for Antarctica.

title: Placing History: How Maps, Spatial Data, and GIS Are Changing Historical Scholarship
creator: Anne Kelly Knowles (ed.)
role_in_essay: Precedent for presenting uncertainty as a finding rather than as a defect.
notes: Supports the Ghost Geographies presentation pattern that ANT-7 is meant to generalise.

title: Royal Museums Greenwich collections record for the southern hemisphere ice chart, G288:1/2(2)
creator: Royal Museums Greenwich
locator: Catalogue record rmgc-object-540947, fields title, object ID, creator, date, scale, credit line
role_in_essay: The evidence for what the 1910 chart compiles and for its Crown copyright credit line.
notes: A catalogue record is a source in its own right and is recorded as one, because it is the only thing about this object that has actually been read. It is not a substitute for the sheet.

title: Royal Museums Greenwich collections record for the 1777 southern hemisphere chart, PAI4123
creator: Royal Museums Greenwich
locator: Catalogue record rmgc-object-154063, fields title, accession number, engraver, date, medium, dimensions
role_in_essay: Establishes the chart's engraver, date and publication context, and that no reuse licence is stated.
notes: Read during the ANT-1 audit. The record names Whitchurch as engraver, which the essay should not silently replace with Cook's name.

short_title: Bergman and Stuart, Location of Endurance
title: On the Location of Shackleton's Vessel Endurance
creator: Lars Bergman and Robin G. Stuart
publication_context: The Journal of Navigation, Cambridge University Press
role_in_essay: The reviewed recomputation of Worsley's observations, and the source the sinking position must be cited from.
notes: The abstract was located during the ANT-9 audit; the article has not been read. It reanalyses Worsley's theodolite and sextant observations from his logbook and reports a sinking position of 68 degrees 39 minutes 30 seconds south, 52 degrees 26 minutes 30 seconds west. This supersedes citing a published narrative for that coordinate, and it means the logbook is reachable through the literature rather than only through an archive visit.

short_title: Bergman, Mearns and Stuart, Chronometer error
title: Influence of chronometer error uncertainties on the Longitude of Shackleton's vessel, Endurance
creator: Lars Bergman, David L. Mearns and Robin G. Stuart
publication_context: The Journal of Navigation, Cambridge University Press
role_in_essay: The uncertainty half of the Coda: what a chronometer error does to a longitude.
notes: Located by search, not read. The year is recorded as an estimate and must be corrected when the article is opened. No uncertainty figure may be published from this project until it is.

title: Why did Endurance sink?
creator: Not recorded
publication_context: Polar Record, volume 61, Cambridge University Press
role_in_essay: Recent scholarship on the loss itself, held in case Act VIII needs it.
notes: Located by search; authors not recorded because the listing did not give them. Peripheral to the navigation argument and included so the act does not overlook current work.

title: Royal Museums Greenwich collections record for the 1874 southern hemisphere ice chart, NTY288:1/2(1)
creator: Royal Museums Greenwich
locator: Catalogue record rmgc-object-555864, fields title, object ID, creators, dates, scale, dimensions, credit line
role_in_essay: The evidence that the cumulative chart was revised, and the voyage list it carried before Scott and Shackleton.
notes: Read during the ANT-8 audit. The 1874 title lists Cook through Ross and adds Towson's papers on icebergs 1855-59; the 1910 sheet adds Scott 1901-4 and Shackleton 1908-9. Two catalogue titles are therefore enough to show a synthesis being revised rather than merely accumulating.

title: Royal Museums Greenwich collections record for the 1777 southern hemisphere chart, G201:3/3
creator: Royal Museums Greenwich
locator: Catalogue record rmgc-object-543571, fields title, object ID, creators, date, dimensions, credit line
role_in_essay: The second Greenwich impression of the 1777 chart, and the attribution the other record does not carry.
notes: Read during the ANT-5 audit. This record names Johann George Forster alongside Whitchurch, which PAI4123 does not, and gives different measurements. Two impressions of one plate, catalogued differently, which is why the essay has to name the copy it reproduces.

short_title: LoC record, US Exploring Expedition atlas
title: Library of Congress record for the Atlas of the Narrative of the United States Exploring Expedition
creator: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division
publication_context: Atlas published Philadelphia: C. Sherman, 1844; digitised copy 3 at shelf g9230m.gct00224
role_in_essay: Locates the Wilkes atlas and its map of the Antarctic continent in a named holding with a digitised copy.
notes: Found by search; the item record itself was not opened. The atlas is reported to contain a map of the Antarctic continent, but the sheet number and the disputed positions on it are still unidentified.

short_title: Dumont d'Urville, Voyage au Pole Sud
title: Voyage au Pole Sud et dans l'Oceanie sur les corvettes l'Astrolabe et la Zelee
creator: Jules Sebastien Cesar Dumont d'Urville
publication_context: Paris: Gide; narrative volumes with an accompanying atlas
role_in_essay: The French contribution to the 1840 season, and a third national account of the same weeks of coast.
notes: Gallica is the likely route to a digitised copy. Neither the volume structure nor the atlas plates have been checked.

short_title: Mill, The Siege of the South Pole
title: The Siege of the South Pole: The Story of Antarctic Exploration
creator: Hugh Robert Mill
role_in_essay: A synthesis of Antarctic knowledge written on the eve of the Heroic Age, and a textual counterpart to the cumulative chart.
notes: Useful precisely because of its date: it shows what a well-informed reader could know in 1905, which is the state the 1910 chart then revises.

short_title: Scott, The Voyage of the Discovery
title: The Voyage of the Discovery
creator: Robert Falcon Scott
publication_context: London: Smith, Elder and Co., two volumes
role_in_essay: One of the two voyages the 1910 chart adds to the 1874 compilation.
notes: Selected for cartographic contribution rather than fame: the Discovery survey is one of the two additions that distinguish the 1910 sheet from its predecessor.

short_title: Shackleton, The Heart of the Antarctic
title: The Heart of the Antarctic
creator: Ernest Shackleton
role_in_essay: The other voyage the 1910 chart adds, and the immediate predecessor of the Endurance plan.
notes: The Nimrod expedition of 1908-9, dated on the 1910 chart's own title.

short_title: Mawson, The Home of the Blizzard
title: The Home of the Blizzard
creator: Douglas Mawson
role_in_essay: Held as a candidate for Act VII on cartographic grounds; the coast charted by the Australasian expedition postdates the 1910 sheet.
notes: Included conditionally. If the act cannot show what his survey added to the map, he should be cut rather than kept for fame.
